proposals: OISD should publish a table of all 121 of its standards and recommended practices showing which are legally binding, under which instrument, and which are guidance only, so operators and the public can see where OISD's authority comes from the 2008 Offshore Rules, PESO adoption, or neither.

PESO should publish the list of OISD standards it has adopted into the Petroleum Rules 2002, with notification references and dates, so the 'roughly a dozen' figure carried by secondary sources is replaced by an official count.

The Bureau of Indian Standards should publish the list of API standards referenced in Indian technical regulations, with the referencing instrument for each, so the count of 90 is available from an Indian source and not only from API's own international usage report.

OISD, PESO and PNGRB should each publish the text and work programme of their MOUs with the American Petroleum Institute, so any change in the weight API standards carry in Indian regulation can be traced to a documented decision.

OISD should publish an annual summary of its safety-audit findings and incident statistics for the installations it audits, so whether India's four-body arrangement works can be judged on incident rates and audit findings rather than on its structure alone.
